mock_data.title: Shift in the Gulf Stream
mock_data.passage:
A New Scientist article by Alec Luhn on how a northward shift in the Gulf Stream could signal a collapse of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation.

A gradual northward shift in the Gulf Stream has provided more evidence that the system of currents that keeps Europe warm is weakening. What's more, modelling suggests that any abrupt shift in the Gulf Stream could signal an imminent, catastrophic collapse in the ocean current.

The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is the flow of warm, salty surface water from the tropics to north-western Europe, where it cools and sinks, returning south along the ocean floor. The part of this circulation running from the Gulf of Mexico up the US east coast to North Carolina, where it veers east into the Atlantic, is called the Gulf Stream.

The AMOC is expected to lose strength as the melting of the Greenland ice sheet dumps fresh water into the north Atlantic, diluting the dense, salty AMOC water and slowing the rate at which it sinks and flows southward. Some research suggests that this is already happening, but scientists don't have direct proof.

Now, a modelling study by René van Westen and Henk Dijkstra, both at Utrecht University in the Netherlands, has shown that a weakening AMOC would shift the path of the Gulf Stream so it follows the US seaboard further north before it veers into the Atlantic.

Moreover, the study finds the Gulf Stream has already shifted northward by about 50 kilometres in 30 years, according to satellite data.

"This is something we can measure," says van Westen. "So it is very likely that this reflects that the AMOC is indeed weakening."

Reconstructions that estimate the AMOC flow rate based on historic sea temperatures suggest it has weakened 15 per cent since 1950. But its actual flow has only been monitored by moored instruments since 2004, not long enough to say whether observed changes are natural fluctuations or a trend.

"Therefore, we are trying to come up with some alternative approaches, such as the Gulf Stream path," says van Westen.

The model in the study represents the world in 10-kilometre pixels rather than the typical 100-kilometre pixels, allowing the researchers to track the bulge where the Gulf Stream is carrying masses of water.

The path of the bulge changes because of the Deep Western Boundary Current, one of the arms of the AMOC carrying cold, salty water southward along the seafloor. This current normally flows down the coast of North America under the Gulf Stream, tugging it to the south. As the AMOC weakens, so does the Deep Western Boundary Current, and the curve of the Gulf Stream gradually shifts northward.

However, 392 years into the simulation's future, the Gulf Stream jumps more than 200 kilometres to the north in just two years. Twenty-five years after that, the AMOC collapses. Previous research has shown that such a collapse would drastically cool Europe; London could see cold snaps of −20°C (−4°F) and Oslo, Norway, could reach −48°C (−54°F).

The modelling is an idealised scenario that does not suggest the AMOC will collapse in 400 years. But it does suggest an abrupt shift in the Gulf Stream could serve as an early warning of an impending AMOC shutdown, the only such prior indicator we know of. While it may be too late at that point to avoid AMOC collapse, Europe could prepare by insulating houses and finding more southerly places to grow food.

"There is now a very proper early warning indicator that actually goes off," says van Westen. "You can measure this very easily."

But it's unclear in the real world how long after a Gulf Stream shift the AMOC could collapse. And projections of when the AMOC might shut down range from decades to centuries.

Dan Seidov, an oceanographer retired from the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, cautions that fresh water from Greenland could "hose" the AMOC at a different rate and in a different place from what the model assumes.

"How, when and why it may or may not happen is the big question," he says. "If it happens as is prescribed in the model, then the Gulf Stream can be a precursor and provide a warning signal."

While the link between the abrupt shift and AMOC collapse will need to be corroborated by other models, this study provides more evidence the AMOC is already slowing, says Stefan Rahmstorf at the University of Potsdam in Germany.

"This slowing is occurring earlier than in the global warming scenarios," he says. "Climate models appear to underestimate the problem and thus potentially how soon an AMOC tipping point will be reached."
mock_data.passageB1:
The Gulf Stream, a strong ocean current, seems to be moving further north. This could be a sign that the system of ocean currents that keeps Europe warm is getting weaker. Scientists are worried that a sudden change in the Gulf Stream could mean that this system is about to collapse.

This system of currents is called the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation, or AMOC for short. It works by carrying warm, salty water from warm areas near the equator towards Europe. As this water travels north, it cools down and becomes heavier. Then, it sinks to the bottom of the ocean and flows back towards the equator. The Gulf Stream is the part of the AMOC that flows from the Gulf of Mexico up the east coast of the United States to North Carolina.

Scientists think the AMOC is getting weaker because the ice in Greenland is melting. This melting ice adds fresh water to the ocean, which makes the water less salty. The less salty water is not as heavy, so it doesn't sink as easily. This slows down the AMOC. Some studies suggest this is already happening, but scientists need more proof.

Two scientists, René van Westen and Henk Dijkstra, used a computer model to study this. They found that if the AMOC gets weaker, the Gulf Stream will move further north along the US coast before turning east into the Atlantic Ocean.

Their study also showed that the Gulf Stream has already moved about 50 kilometres north in the last 30 years, based on information from satellites.

Van Westen said that this movement is something they can measure. He believes it is likely a sign that the AMOC is getting weaker.

Scientists have also looked at old sea temperatures to estimate how strong the AMOC was in the past. These estimates suggest that the AMOC has weakened by 15% since 1950. However, they have only been using special tools to directly monitor the AMOC since 2004. This is not long enough to know if the changes they see are just normal changes or a long-term trend.

Van Westen said that they are trying to find other ways to study the AMOC, like looking at the path of the Gulf Stream.

The computer model used in the study showed the world in small squares, each 10 kilometres wide. This helped the scientists track the Gulf Stream and see how it moves.

The Gulf Stream's path changes because of another current called the Deep Western Boundary Current. This current is part of the AMOC and carries cold, salty water south along the ocean floor. It usually flows under the Gulf Stream and pulls it south. But if the AMOC gets weaker, the Deep Western Boundary Current also gets weaker. This means the Gulf Stream can move further north.

In the model, the Gulf Stream suddenly moved more than 200 kilometres north in just two years. This happened 392 years into the future in the model. Then, 25 years later, the AMOC collapsed. Other studies have shown that if the AMOC collapses, Europe could become much colder. For example, London could have temperatures as low as -20°C, and Oslo, Norway, could reach -48°C.

The model is a simplified scenario and doesn't mean the AMOC will collapse in 400 years. However, it suggests that a sudden shift in the Gulf Stream could be a warning sign that the AMOC is about to shut down. This could give Europe time to prepare, such as by making houses warmer and finding new places to grow food.

Van Westen said that this sudden shift is like an early warning that they can easily detect.

However, scientists are not sure how long it would take for the AMOC to collapse after the Gulf Stream shifts. Some think it could be decades, while others think it could be centuries.

Dan Seidov, an oceanographer, warned that fresh water from Greenland could affect the AMOC in a different way than the model predicts.

He said that the big question is how, when, and why the AMOC might collapse. If it happens as the model suggests, then the Gulf Stream could be a warning sign.

Stefan Rahmstorf, another scientist, said that this study provides more evidence that the AMOC is already slowing down. He added that other models should also confirm the link between the Gulf Stream shift and the AMOC collapse.

He also said that the AMOC is slowing down faster than expected in global warming scenarios. He thinks that climate models may not fully understand the problem and may not be able to estimate when the AMOC might reach a tipping point.
mock_data.passageB2:
Scientists are becoming increasingly concerned about a change in the Gulf Stream, a major ocean current. A recent article in New Scientist by Alec Luhn suggests that a shift of the Gulf Stream further north could be a sign that the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC), a crucial system of ocean currents, is on the verge of collapse.

The article highlights evidence that the Gulf Stream is gradually moving northward. This movement supports the idea that the AMOC, which plays a vital role in maintaining Europe's relatively mild climate, is weakening. Furthermore, computer models indicate that a sudden shift in the Gulf Stream's path could foreshadow an imminent and disastrous collapse of the entire ocean current system.

The AMOC functions like a giant conveyor belt, transporting warm, salty water from the tropics towards north-western Europe. As this water reaches colder regions, it cools, becomes denser, and sinks to the ocean floor, eventually flowing back south. The Gulf Stream is the part of this system that travels from the Gulf of Mexico along the east coast of the United States up to North Carolina, where it then turns eastward into the Atlantic Ocean. Its normal trajectory is therefore critical to the overall AMOC function.

Experts predict that the AMOC will weaken as the Greenland ice sheet melts, releasing large amounts of fresh water into the North Atlantic. This influx of fresh water dilutes the salty water that drives the AMOC, reducing its density and slowing down the sinking process. While some studies suggest this process is already underway, definitive proof has been elusive.

However, a new study by René van Westen and Henk Dijkstra at Utrecht University in the Netherlands provides further insight. Their computer model shows that a weakening AMOC would cause the Gulf Stream to shift, following the US coastline further north before turning into the Atlantic. This deviation from its normal path is a key indicator.

According to satellite data, the study also reveals that the Gulf Stream has already shifted northward by approximately 50 kilometres over the past 30 years.

Van Westen explains, "This is something we can measure. Therefore, it is highly probable that this reflects the weakening of the AMOC."

Historical data, based on sea temperature records, estimates that the AMOC's flow rate has decreased by 15% since 1950. However, direct monitoring of the AMOC's flow using instruments has only been in place since 2004, which is not long enough to determine whether the observed changes are natural variations or a long-term trend.

"Therefore, we are trying to develop alternative methods, such as observing the path of the Gulf Stream," says van Westen.

The computer model used in the study represents the world using 10-kilometre units, allowing the researchers to monitor the bulge of water carried by the Gulf Stream with greater precision than typical models that use 100-kilometre units.

The path of this bulge changes due to the Deep Western Boundary Current, a component of the AMOC that transports cold, salty water southward along the ocean floor. This current usually flows beneath the Gulf Stream along the North American coast, pulling it southward. As the AMOC weakens, so does the Deep Western Boundary Current, causing the Gulf Stream's curve to gradually shift northward. This interaction is fundamental to understanding the shift.

However, in the model's simulation, 392 years into the future, the Gulf Stream suddenly jumps more than 200 kilometres northward within just two years. Twenty-five years later, the AMOC collapses. Previous studies have shown that such a collapse would dramatically cool Europe, potentially leading to extreme cold weather events. This extreme scenario highlights the potential consequences.

While the model presents an idealised scenario and does not predict an AMOC collapse in 400 years, it does suggest that a sudden shift in the Gulf Stream could serve as an early warning sign of an impending AMOC shutdown. This could provide valuable time for Europe to prepare by improving insulation in homes and identifying more suitable locations for food production. This preparation can mitigate the worst impacts.

"There is now a very clear early warning indicator that actually activates," says van Westen. "You can measure this very easily."

However, it remains unclear how much time would pass between a Gulf Stream shift and an AMOC collapse in the real world. Projections for when the AMOC might shut down range from decades to centuries. The uncertainty surrounding the timing is a key challenge.

Dan Seidov, a retired oceanographer from the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, cautions that fresh water from Greenland could affect the AMOC at a different rate and in a different location than the model assumes. This complexity makes predictions difficult.

"How, when, and why it may or may not happen is the big question," he says. "If it happens as is prescribed in the model, then the Gulf Stream can be a precursor and provide a warning signal."

While the link between the abrupt shift and AMOC collapse needs to be confirmed by other models, this study adds to the growing evidence that the AMOC is already slowing down, according to Stefan Rahmstorf at the University of Potsdam in Germany. Further investigation is needed.

"This slowing is occurring earlier than in the global warming scenarios," he says. "Climate models appear to underestimate the problem and thus potentially how soon an AMOC tipping point will be reached."
mock_data.passageC1:
Mounting evidence suggests a northward migration of the Gulf Stream, a phenomenon that, according to a recent New Scientist article by Alec Luhn, could presage the weakening, or even the collapse, of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC), the very ocean current system responsible for Europe's relatively temperate climate. Indeed, modelling indicates that any abrupt alteration in the Gulf Stream's trajectory might serve as an ominous harbinger of an impending, and potentially catastrophic, breakdown in this crucial oceanic conveyor belt.

The AMOC functions as a complex circulatory system, transporting warm, saline surface waters from the tropics towards north-western Europe. Here, the water releases heat, cools, and subsequently sinks, forming a dense, cold current that flows southward along the ocean floor. The Gulf Stream represents a crucial segment of this larger circulation, originating in the Gulf of Mexico and coursing up the eastern seaboard of the United States to North Carolina, before veering eastward into the open Atlantic.

A decline in the AMOC's strength is anticipated as a consequence of the Greenland ice sheet's melting, an event that introduces substantial quantities of fresh water into the North Atlantic. This influx dilutes the dense, salty water crucial for the AMOC's sinking process, thereby impeding its flow rate. While some investigations intimate that this weakening is already underway, definitive, irrefutable evidence has, thus far, remained elusive.

However, a recent modelling study conducted by René van Westen and Henk Dijkstra at Utrecht University in the Netherlands, posits that a weakened AMOC would induce a shift in the Gulf Stream's path, causing it to adhere more closely to the US coastline before deflecting towards the Atlantic. The implications of this subtle, yet potentially significant, change are far-reaching.

Further bolstering this hypothesis, the study reveals that, based on satellite data, the Gulf Stream has already shifted northward by approximately 50 kilometers over the past three decades. This observed shift, as van Westen notes, is a tangible phenomenon that can be measured, making it a plausible indicator of a genuine weakening of the AMOC.

Historical reconstructions, which estimate the AMOC's flow rate based on past sea temperatures, suggest a 15 percent reduction in its strength since 1950. Nevertheless, direct monitoring of the AMOC's actual flow, using moored instruments, only commenced in 2004. This relatively short observational period renders it challenging to discern whether the observed changes represent natural, cyclical fluctuations or a more insidious trend.

“Therefore, we are trying to come up with some alternative approaches, such as the Gulf Stream path,” says van Westen, underscoring the need for corroborating evidence beyond direct flow measurements.

The model employed in the study utilizes a high-resolution grid, representing the world in 10-kilometer pixels, a significant improvement over the more common 100-kilometer resolution. This enhanced resolution enables the researchers to accurately track the bulge formed by the Gulf Stream as it transports vast quantities of water. The meandering course of this bulge is intricately linked to the Deep Western Boundary Current, a component of the AMOC responsible for carrying cold, salty water southward along the seafloor.

This deep current normally flows beneath the Gulf Stream, exerting a southward pull on it. As the AMOC weakens, so too does the Deep Western Boundary Current, resulting in a gradual northward shift of the Gulf Stream's curvature. The study highlights the complex interplay of forces at work within this oceanic system.

Intriguingly, the simulation projects that, 392 years into the future, the Gulf Stream undergoes an abrupt northward jump of over 200 kilometers in just two years. A mere 25 years later, the AMOC collapses entirely. Prior research has demonstrated that such a collapse would precipitate a dramatic cooling across Europe, potentially subjecting London to cold snaps reaching −20°C (−4°F) and Oslo, Norway, to temperatures as low as −48°C (−54°F). The potential ramifications are thus, severe.

It is crucial to acknowledge that this modelling exercise represents an idealized scenario and should not be interpreted as a definitive prediction of an AMOC collapse within the next four centuries. Rather, it suggests that an abrupt shift in the Gulf Stream could serve as an early warning signal of an impending AMOC shutdown. Even if such a warning arrives too late to avert the collapse entirely, it could afford Europe valuable time to prepare, for example, by improving insulation in buildings and identifying more suitable locations for agriculture.

“There is now a very proper early warning indicator that actually goes off,” says van Westen. “You can measure this very easily,” underscoring the accessibility and potential utility of this indicator.

However, the precise timeframe between a Gulf Stream shift and a subsequent AMOC collapse remains uncertain in the real world. Projections regarding the timing of a potential AMOC shutdown vary considerably, ranging from decades to centuries. The exact causal relationship is still being studied.

Dan Seidov, a retired oceanographer from the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, cautions that the rate and location at which fresh water from Greenland enters the system could differ significantly from the model's assumptions, potentially skewing the results.

“How, when and why it may or may not happen is the big question,” he says. “If it happens as is prescribed in the model, then the Gulf Stream can be a precursor and provide a warning signal.” The predictive power of the Gulf Stream shift, therefore, hinges on the accuracy of the model's underlying assumptions.

While the link between an abrupt Gulf Stream shift and AMOC collapse requires further validation through additional models, this study provides yet more evidence that the AMOC is already slowing, according to Stefan Rahmstorf at the University of Potsdam in Germany. This gradual deceleration is happening earlier than anticipated in global warming scenarios.

“This slowing is occurring earlier than in the global warming scenarios,” he says. “Climate models appear to underestimate the problem and thus potentially how soon an AMOC tipping point will be reached,” highlighting the urgent need for continued research and monitoring of this vital oceanic system.

mock_data.translation:
Alek Lun tomonidan yozilgan New Scientist maqolasi — Golf oqimining shimolga siljishi Atlantika meridional aylanma oqimining qulab tushishiga qanday ishora qilishi mumkinligi haqida.

Golf oqimining asta-sekin shimolga siljishi Yevropani iliq ushlab turadigan oqimlar tizimi kuchsizlanayotganiga yana bir dalil berdi. Bundan tashqari, modellashtirish shuni ko'rsatadiki, Golf oqimidagi har qanday to'satdan siljish okean oqimining yaqin kelajakdagi halokatli qulab tushishiga ishora qilishi mumkin.

Atlantika meridional aylanma oqimi (AMOC) — tropik hududlardan shimoliy-g'arbiy Yevropaga issiq, sho'r suv oqimi bo'lib, u yerda soviydi va cho'kadi, keyin okean tubidan janubga qaytadi. Bu aylanma oqimning Meksika ko'rfazidan AQSh sharqiy qirg'og'i bo'ylab Shimoliy Karolinagacha, u yerdan Atlantikaga buriladigan qismi Golf oqimi deb ataladi.

Grenlandiya muz qatlamining erishi shimoliy Atlantikaga chuchuk suv tashlagani sababli AMOCning kuchsizlanishi kutilmoqda, bu zich, sho'r AMOC suvini suyultiradi va uning cho'kish va janubga oqish tezligini sekinlashtiradi. Ba'zi tadqiqotlar bu allaqachon sodir bo'layotganini ko'rsatadi, ammo olimlar bevosita dalilga ega emaslar.

Endi, Niderlandiyadagi Utrext universitetidagi René van Vesten va Xenk Deykstra tomonidan olib borilgan modellashtirish tadqiqoti, kuchsizlanayotgan AMOC Golf oqimining yo'lini o'zgartirishini ko'rsatdi, shunda u Atlantikaga burilishdan oldin AQSh qirg'og'i bo'ylab shimolga yaqinroq davom etadi.

Bundan tashqari, tadqiqot Golf oqimi sun'iy yo'ldosh ma'lumotlariga ko'ra 30 yil ichida taxminan 50 kilometrga shimolga siljganini aniqladi.

"Bu biz o'lchay oladigan narsa," deydi van Vesten. "Shuning uchun bu AMOC haqiqatan ham kuchsizlanayotganini aks ettirishining ehtimoli juda yuqori."

Tarixiy dengiz haroratlariga asoslangan AMOC oqim tezligini baholaydigan rekonstruktsiyalar u 1950-yildan beri 15 foizga kuchsizlanganini ko'rsatadi. Ammo uning haqiqiy oqimi faqat 2004-yildan beri langarlangan asboblar bilan kuzatilmoqda, bu kuzatilgan o'zgarishlar tabiiy tebranishlarmi yoki tendentsiyami deyish uchun yetarli emas.

"Shuning uchun biz Golf oqimi yo'li kabi muqobil yondashuvlarni ishlab chiqishga harakat qilmoqdamiz," deydi van Vesten.

Tadqiqotdagi model dunyoni odatiy 100 kilometrli piksellar o'rniga 10 kilometrli piksellarda ifodalaydi, bu tadqiqotchilarga Golf oqimi suv massalarini tashiyotgan bo'rtmani kuzatish imkonini beradi.

Bo'rtmaning yo'li Chuqur G'arbiy Chegara Oqimi tufayli o'zgaradi — AMOCning sovuq, sho'r suvni okean tubi bo'ylab janubga tashiyotgan qo'llaridan biri. Bu oqim odatda Shimoliy Amerikaning qirg'og'i bo'ylab Golf oqimi ostida janubga oqadi va uni janubga tortadi. AMOC kuchsizlanganda, Chuqur G'arbiy Chegara Oqimi ham kuchsizlanadi va Golf oqimining egri chizig'i asta-sekin shimolga siljiydi.

Biroq, simulyatsiyaning kelajagiga 392 yil o'tgach, Golf oqimi atigi ikki yil ichida 200 kilometrdan ko'proq shimolga sakraydi. Bundan yigirma besh yil keyin AMOC qulab tushadi. Oldingi tadqiqotlar bunday qulab tushish Yevropani keskin sovitishini ko'rsatgan; London −20°C (−4°F) sovuq to'lqinlarini ko'rishi mumkin va Norvegiyaning Oslo shahri −48°C (−54°F) ga yetishi mumkin.

Modellashtirish AMOCning 400 yil ichida qulab tushishini ko'rsatmaydigan ideallashtirilgan ssenariy. Ammo u Golf oqimidagi to'satdan siljish yaqinlashib kelayotgan AMOC to'xtashi haqida erta ogohlantirish bo'lib xizmat qilishi mumkinligini ko'rsatadi — bu biz bilgan yagona bunday oldingi ko'rsatkich. Bu nuqtada AMOC qulab tushishining oldini olish uchun juda kech bo'lishi mumkin bo'lsa-da, Yevropa uylarni izolyatsiya qilish va oziq-ovqat yetishtirish uchun janubiyroq joylarni topish orqali tayyorgarlik ko'rishi mumkin.

"Endi haqiqatan ham ishga tushadigan juda to'g'ri erta ogohlantirish ko'rsatkichi bor," deydi van Vesten. "Buni juda oson o'lchash mumkin."

Ammo real dunyoda Golf oqimi siljishidan keyin AMOC qachon qulab tushishi mumkinligi noaniq. Va AMOCning qachon to'xtashi mumkinligi bo'yicha prognozlar o'n yilliklardan asrlargacha.

AQSh Milliy okean va atmosfera boshqarmasidan nafaqaga chiqqan okeanograf Den Seydov Grenlandiyadan kelayotgan chuchuk suv AMOCni model taxmin qilganidan boshqa tezlikda va boshqa joyda "yuvishi" mumkinligini ogohlantiradi.

"Bu qachon, qanday va nima uchun sodir bo'lishi yoki bo'lmasligi katta savol," deydi u. "Agar u modelda belgilangandek sodir bo'lsa, Golf oqimi oldindan xabar beruvchi bo'lishi va ogohlantirish signalini berishi mumkin."

To'satdan siljish va AMOC qulab tushishi o'rtasidagi bog'liqlik boshqa modellar tomonidan tasdiqlanishi kerak bo'lsa-da, bu tadqiqot AMOC allaqachon sekinlashayotganiga ko'proq dalil beradi, deydi Germaniyaning Potsdam universitetidagi Stefan Ramshtorf.

"Bu sekinlashish global isish ssenariylaridagidan ertaroq sodir bo'lmoqda," deydi u. "Iqlim modellari muammoni va shuning uchun AMOC burilish nuqtasiga qanchalik tez yetib borishini kam baholamoqda."

mock_data.translationB1:
Kuchli okean oqimi bo'lgan Golfstrim shimolga qarab siljiyotganga o'xshaydi. Bu Yevropani iliq saqlaydigan okean oqimlari tizimi zaiflashayotganining belgisi bo'lishi mumkin. Olimlar Golfstrimda keskin o'zgarish bo'lishi bu tizimning qulashi arafasida ekanligidan xavotirda.

Bu oqimlar tizimi Atlantika meridional aylanish sirkulyatsiyasi yoki qisqacha AMOK deb ataladi. U ekvatorga yaqin iliq hududlardan Yevropaga iliq, sho'r suvni olib o'tish orqali ishlaydi. Bu suv shimolga qarab harakatlanar ekan, soviydi va og'irlashadi. Keyin u okean tubiga cho'kib, ekvatorga qarab oqib ketadi. Golfstrim - bu Meksika qo'ltig'idan AQShning sharqiy qirg'og'i bo'ylab Shimoliy Karolinagacha oqadigan AMOKning bir qismidir.

Olimlarning fikricha, Grenlandiyadagi muzliklar erishi tufayli AMOK zaiflashmoqda. Bu erigan muz okeanga chuchuk suv qo'shadi, bu esa suvni kamroq sho'r qiladi. Kamroq sho'r suv unchalik og'ir emas, shuning uchun u osonlikcha cho'kmaydi. Bu AMOKning sekinlashishiga olib keladi. Ba'zi tadqiqotlar bu allaqachon sodir bo'layotganini ko'rsatadi, ammo olimlarga ko'proq dalil kerak.

Ikki olim, Rene van Westen va Henk Deykstra, buni kompyuter modeli yordamida o'rganishdi. Ular agar AMOK zaiflashsa, Golfstrim AQSh qirg'og'i bo'ylab sharqqa Atlantika okeaniga burilishidan oldin shimolga siljishini aniqladilar.

Ularning tadqiqoti shuni ko'rsatdiki, Golfstrim sun'iy yo'ldoshlardan olingan ma'lumotlarga asoslanib, so'nggi 30 yil ichida allaqachon taxminan 50 kilometr shimolga siljigan.

Van Westenning aytishicha, bu harakatni o'lchash mumkin. Uning fikricha, bu, ehtimol, AMOKning zaiflashayotganidan dalolat beradi.

Olimlar, shuningdek, AMOKning o'tmishda qanchalik kuchli bo'lganini baholash uchun eski dengiz haroratlariga qarashdi. Bu baholar AMOK 1950 yildan beri 15% ga zaiflashganini ko'rsatadi. Biroq, ular AMOKni bevosita kuzatish uchun maxsus asboblardan faqat 2004 yildan beri foydalanmoqdalar. Bu ular ko'rayotgan o'zgarishlar oddiy o'zgarishlarmi yoki uzoq muddatli tendentsiyami, bilish uchun etarli emas.

Van Westenning aytishicha, ular Golfstrim yo'liga qarash kabi AMOKni o'rganishning boshqa usullarini topishga harakat qilmoqdalar.

Tadqiqotda ishlatilgan kompyuter modeli dunyoni har biri 10 kilometr kenglikdagi kichik kvadratlarda ko'rsatdi. Bu olimlarga Golfstrimni kuzatishga va uning qanday harakatlanishini ko'rishga yordam berdi.

Golfstrim yo'li G'arbiy Chuqur Chegara Oqimi deb ataladigan boshqa oqim tufayli o'zgaradi. Bu oqim AMOKning bir qismi bo'lib, okean tubi bo'ylab sovuq, sho'r suvni janubga olib o'tadi. Odatda u Golfstrim ostidan oqadi va uni janubga tortadi. Ammo agar AMOK zaiflashsa, G'arbiy Chuqur Chegara Oqimi ham zaiflashadi. Bu Golfstrimning shimolga siljishiga imkon beradi.

Modelda Golfstrim atigi ikki yil ichida birdaniga 200 kilometrdan ortiq shimolga siljidi. Bu modelda kelajakda 392 yil o'tgach sodir bo'ldi. Keyin, 25 yildan so'ng, AMOK quladi. Boshqa tadqiqotlar shuni ko'rsatdiki, agar AMOK qulasa, Yevropa ancha sovuq bo'lishi mumkin. Masalan, Londonda harorat -20°C gacha, Norvegiyaning Oslo shahrida esa -48°C gacha tushishi mumkin.

Model soddalashtirilgan stsenariy bo'lib, bu AMOK 400 yildan keyin qulaydi degani emas. Biroq, bu Golfstrimdagi keskin siljish AMOKning o'chishi arafasida ekanligining ogohlantiruvchi belgisi bo'lishi mumkinligini ko'rsatadi. Bu Yevropaga uylarni isitish va oziq-ovqat yetishtirish uchun yangi joylar topish kabi tayyorgarlik ko'rish uchun vaqt berishi mumkin.

Van Westenning aytishicha, bu keskin siljish - bu ular osonlikcha aniqlay oladigan erta ogohlantirishga o'xshaydi.

Biroq, olimlar Golfstrim siljiganidan keyin AMOKning qulashi qancha vaqt olishiga amin emaslar. Ba'zilarning fikricha, bu o'n yillar, boshqalarning fikricha, asrlar bo'lishi mumkin.

Okeanograf Den Seidov Grenlandiyadan keladigan chuchuk suv AMOKga model bashorat qilganidan farqli ravishda ta'sir qilishi mumkinligi haqida ogohlantirdi.

Uning aytishicha, asosiy savol AMOK qanday, qachon va nima uchun qulashi mumkinligi. Agar u modelda ko'rsatilgandek sodir bo'lsa, Golfstrim ogohlantiruvchi belgi bo'lishi mumkin.

Boshqa bir olim Stefan Ramstorfning aytishicha, bu tadqiqot AMOKning allaqachon sekinlashayotganiga ko'proq dalil keltiradi. Uning qo'shimcha qilishicha, boshqa modellar ham Golfstrim siljishi va AMOKning qulashi o'rtasidagi bog'liqlikni tasdiqlashi kerak.

U, shuningdek, AMOK global isish stsenariylarida kutilganidan tezroq sekinlashayotganini aytdi. Uning fikricha, iqlim modellari muammoni to'liq tushunmasligi va AMOK qachon burilish nuqtasiga yetishini baholay olmasligi mumkin.
mock_data.translationB2:
Olimlar asosiy okean oqimi bo'lgan Golfstrimda yuz berayotgan o'zgarishdan tobora ko'proq xavotirda. Alek Lunning New Scientist jurnalidagi yaqinda chop etilgan maqolasida Golfstrimning shimolga siljishi okean oqimlarining muhim tizimi bo'lgan Atlantika Meridional Ag'darilish Sirkulatsiyasi (AMOC) qulash arafasida ekanligining belgisi bo'lishi mumkinligi aytilgan.

Maqolada Golfstrimning asta-sekin shimolga qarab harakatlanayotganiga oid dalillar keltirilgan. Bu harakat Yevropaning nisbatan mo''tadil iqlimini saqlashda muhim rol o'ynaydigan AMOCning zaiflashayotgani haqidagi fikrni qo'llab-quvvatlaydi. Bundan tashqari, kompyuter modellari Golfstrim yo'nalishining to'satdan o'zgarishi butun okean oqimi tizimining tez orada ro'y beradigan va halokatli qulashidan ogohlantirishi mumkinligini ko'rsatadi.

AMOC xuddi ulkan konveyer lentasi kabi ishlaydi va tropiklardan shimoli-g'arbiy Yevropaga iliq, sho'r suvni tashib beradi. Bu suv sovuq hududlarga yetib borgach, soviydi, zichroq bo'ladi va okean tubiga cho'kadi, oxir-oqibat yana janubga oqadi. Golfstrim bu tizimning Meksika ko'rfazidan Qo'shma Shtatlarning sharqiy qirg'og'i bo'ylab Shimoliy Karolinagacha bo'lgan qismi bo'lib, u yerda sharqqa Atlantika okeaniga buriladi. Shuning uchun uning odatiy trayektoriyasi AMOCning umumiy faoliyati uchun juda muhim.

Mutaxassislarning fikricha, Grenlandiya muz qatlami erishi natijasida Shimoliy Atlantikaga ko'p miqdorda chuchuk suv tushishi bilan AMOC zaiflashadi. Ushbu chuchuk suv oqimi AMOCni harakatga keltiradigan sho'r suvni suyultiradi, uning zichligini pasaytiradi va cho'kish jarayonini sekinlashtiradi. Ba'zi tadqiqotlar bu jarayon allaqachon boshlanganini ko'rsatsa-da, aniq isbot hali topilmadi.

Biroq, Niderlandiyadagi Utrext universitetidan Rene van Westen va Henk Deykstraning yangi tadqiqoti qo'shimcha ma'lumot beradi. Ularning kompyuter modeli shuni ko'rsatadiki, AMOCning zaiflashishi Golfstrimning AQSh qirg'oq chizig'i bo'ylab shimolga siljishiga, so'ngra Atlantikaga burilishiga olib keladi. Uning odatiy yo'nalishidan bu og'ishi asosiy ko'rsatkichdir.

Sun'iy yo'ldosh ma'lumotlariga ko'ra, tadqiqot shuni ham ko'rsatadiki, Golfstrim so'nggi 30 yil ichida taxminan 50 kilometrga shimolga siljigan.

Van Westen shunday deb tushuntiradi: "Bu biz o'lchay oladigan narsa. Shuning uchun, bu AMOCning zaiflashishini aks ettirishi juda ehtimolli".

Dengiz harorati yozuvlariga asoslangan tarixiy ma'lumotlar shuni ko'rsatadiki, AMOCning oqim tezligi 1950 yildan beri 15% ga kamaygan. Biroq, asboblar yordamida AMOC oqimini bevosita kuzatish faqat 2004 yildan beri mavjud, bu kuzatilgan o'zgarishlar tabiiy o'zgarishlarmi yoki uzoq muddatli tendentsiyami, aniqlash uchun yetarli emas.

"Shuning uchun biz Golfstrim yo'lini kuzatish kabi muqobil usullarni ishlab chiqishga harakat qilyapmiz", deydi van Westen.

Tadqiqotda ishlatilgan kompyuter modeli dunyoni 10 kilometrlik birliklardan foydalangan holda ifodalaydi, bu esa tadqiqotchilarga Golfstrim tomonidan olib boriladigan suvning bo'rtiqini 100 kilometrlik birliklardan foydalanadigan odatiy modellarga qaraganda aniqroq kuzatishga imkon beradi.

Ushbu bo'rtiqning yo'li AMOCning tarkibiy qismi bo'lgan chuqur g'arbiy chegara oqimi tufayli o'zgaradi, u sovuq, sho'r suvni okean tubi bo'ylab janubga tashlaydi. Bu oqim odatda Shimoliy Amerika qirg'og'i bo'ylab Golfstrim ostidan oqib o'tadi va uni janubga tortadi. AMOC zaiflashganda, chuqur g'arbiy chegara oqimi ham zaiflashadi, bu esa Golfstrim egri chizig'ining asta-sekin shimolga siljishiga olib keladi. Ushbu o'zaro ta'sir siljishni tushunish uchun asosiy hisoblanadi.

Biroq, modelning simulyatsiyasida kelajakda 392 yildan so'ng Golfstrim atigi ikki yil ichida birdaniga 200 kilometrdan ortiq shimolga sakraydi. Yigirma besh yil o'tgach, AMOC qulaydi. Oldingi tadqiqotlar shuni ko'rsatdiki, bunday qulash Yevropani keskin sovutib, ekstremal sovuq ob-havo hodisalariga olib kelishi mumkin. Ushbu favqulodda ssenariy potentsial oqibatlarni ko'rsatadi.

Model ideal ssenariyni taqdim etsa ham va 400 yil ichida AMOCning qulashini bashorat qilmasa ham, Golfstrimdagi to'satdan siljish AMOCning yaqinlashib kelayotgan to'xtashining erta ogohlantirish belgisi bo'lishi mumkinligini ko'rsatadi. Bu Yevropaga uylarning izolyatsiyasini yaxshilash va oziq-ovqat ishlab chiqarish uchun yanada mos joylarni aniqlash orqali tayyorgarlik ko'rish uchun qimmatli vaqt berishi mumkin. Bu tayyorgarlik eng yomon oqibatlarni yumshatishi mumkin.

"Endi haqiqatan ham faollashadigan juda aniq erta ogohlantirish ko'rsatkichi mavjud", deydi van Westen. "Buni juda oson o'lchashingiz mumkin."

AQSh Milliy okean va atmosfera boshqarmasining nafaqadagi okeanografi Den Seidov Grenlandiyadan keladigan chuchuk suv AMOCga modelda taxmin qilinganidan farqli tezlikda va boshqa joyda ta'sir qilishi mumkinligi haqida ogohlantiradi. Ushbu murakkablik prognozlarni qiyinlashtiradi.

To'satdan siljish va AMOCning qulashi o'rtasidagi bog'liqlik boshqa modellar tomonidan tasdiqlanishi kerak bo'lsa-da, bu tadqiqot Germaniyaning Potsdam universitetidan Stefan Ramstorffning fikriga ko'ra, AMOC allaqachon sekinlashayotganiga oid o'sib borayotgan dalillarga qo'shiladi. Qo'shimcha tekshiruv zarur.

"Bu sekinlashish global isish ssenariylariga qaraganda erta sodir bo'lmoqda", deydi u. "Iqlim modellari muammoni va shuning uchun AMOCning burilish nuqtasi qanchalik tez yetib borilishini kam baholaydi, shekilli."

O‘tmishdagi dengiz haroratiga asoslangan holda AMOC oqim tezligini baholaydigan tarixiy rekonstruksiyalar 1950-yildan beri uning kuchida 15 foizga kamayishni ko‘rsatadi.
